blocks.en_text: Are you sleeping restlessly,
blocks.zh_text: 你是不是睡得不安稳，

blocks.en_text: feeling irritable or moody,
blocks.zh_text: 容易烦躁或情绪低落，

blocks.en_text: forgetting little things,
blocks.zh_text: 忘掉一些小事，

blocks.en_text: and feeling overwhelmed and isolated?
blocks.zh_text: 还感到不堪重负、孤立无援？

blocks.en_text: Don't worry. We've all been there.
blocks.zh_text: 别担心，我们都经历过。

blocks.en_text: You're probably just stressed out.
blocks.zh_text: 你大概只是压力太大了。

blocks.en_text: Stress isn't always a bad thing.
blocks.zh_text: 压力并不总是坏事。

blocks.en_text: It can be handy for a burst of extra energy and focus,
blocks.zh_text: 它能帮你瞬间爆发出额外的精力和专注力，

blocks.en_text: like when you're playing a competitive sport,
blocks.zh_text: 比如你在打一场竞技比赛时，

blocks.en_text: or have to speak in public.
blocks.zh_text: 或者不得不在公众面前讲话时。

blocks.en_text: But when its continuous,
blocks.zh_text: 但当压力持续不断，

blocks.en_text: the kind most of us face day in and day out,
blocks.zh_text: 也就是我们大多数人日复一日面对的那种，

blocks.en_text: it actually begins to change your brain.
blocks.zh_text: 它其实就开始改变你的大脑了。

blocks.en_text: Chronic stress,
blocks.zh_text: 长期压力，

blocks.en_text: like being overworked or having arguments at home,
blocks.zh_text: 比如过度劳累或在家里争吵，

blocks.en_text: can affect brain size,
blocks.zh_text: 会影响大脑的大小、

blocks.en_text: its structure,
blocks.zh_text: 它的结构，

blocks.en_text: and how it functions,
blocks.zh_text: 以及它的运作方式，

blocks.en_text: right down to the level of your genes.
blocks.zh_text: 甚至一直影响到你的基因层面。

blocks.en_text: Stress begins with something called
blocks.zh_text: 压力始于一个叫做

blocks.en_text: the hypothalamus pituitary adrenal axis,
blocks.zh_text: 下丘脑—垂体—肾上腺轴的东西，

blocks.en_text: a series of interactions
blocks.zh_text: 它是一系列相互作用，

blocks.en_text: between endocrine glands in the brain and on the kidney,
blocks.zh_text: 发生在脑部和肾脏的内分泌腺之间，

blocks.en_text: which controls your body's reaction to stress.
blocks.zh_text: 它控制着你身体对压力的反应。

blocks.en_text: When your brain detects a stressful situation,
blocks.zh_text: 当你的大脑察觉到压力情境时，

blocks.en_text: your HPA axis is instantly activated
blocks.zh_text: 你的HPA轴会立刻被激活，

blocks.en_text: and releases a hormone called cortisol, which primes your body for instant action.
blocks.zh_text: 并释放一种叫皮质醇的激素，让你的身体做好立即行动的准备。

blocks.en_text: But high levels of cortisol over long periods of time
blocks.zh_text: 但皮质醇长期处于高水平

blocks.en_text: wreak havoc on your brain.
blocks.zh_text: 会对你的大脑造成严重破坏。

blocks.en_text: For example, chronic stress increases the activity level
blocks.zh_text: 例如，长期压力会提高

blocks.en_text: and number of neural connections in the amygdala,
blocks.zh_text: 杏仁核中神经连接的活动水平和数量，

blocks.en_text: your brain's fear center.
blocks.zh_text: 杏仁核是你大脑的恐惧中心。

blocks.en_text: And as levels of cortisol rise,
blocks.zh_text: 而随着皮质醇水平升高，

blocks.en_text: electric signals in your hippocampus,
blocks.zh_text: 你海马体中的电信号，

blocks.en_text: the part of the brain associated with learning, memories, and stress control,
blocks.zh_text: 海马体是大脑中与学习、记忆和压力控制相关的部分，

blocks.en_text: deteriorate.
blocks.zh_text: 会逐渐退化。

blocks.en_text: The hippocampus also inhibits the activity of the HPA axis,
blocks.zh_text: 海马体还会抑制HPA轴的活动，

blocks.en_text: so when it weakens,
blocks.zh_text: 所以当它变弱时，

blocks.en_text: so does your ability to control your stress.
blocks.zh_text: 你控制压力的能力也会变弱。

blocks.en_text: That's not all, though.
blocks.zh_text: 不过，这还不是全部。

blocks.en_text: Cortisol can literally cause your brain to shrink in size.
blocks.zh_text: 皮质醇真的能让你的大脑体积缩小。

blocks.en_text: Too much of it results in the loss of synaptic connections between neurons
blocks.zh_text: 皮质醇过多会导致神经元之间的突触连接丧失，

blocks.en_text: and the shrinking of your prefrontal cortex,
blocks.zh_text: 以及你的前额叶皮层萎缩，

blocks.en_text: the part of your brain the regulates behaviors like concentration,
blocks.zh_text: 前额叶皮层是大脑中调节专注力等行为的部分，

blocks.en_text: decision-making,
blocks.zh_text: 决策、

blocks.en_text: judgement,
blocks.zh_text: 判断，

blocks.en_text: and social interaction.
blocks.zh_text: 以及社交互动。

blocks.en_text: It also leads to fewer new brain cells being made in the hippocampus.
blocks.zh_text: 它还会导致海马体中生成的新脑细胞减少。

blocks.en_text: This means chronic stress might make it harder for you to learn
blocks.zh_text: 这意味着长期压力可能会让你更难学习

blocks.en_text: and remember things,
blocks.zh_text: 和记住东西，

blocks.en_text: and also set the stage for more serious mental problems,
blocks.zh_text: 还会为更严重的心理问题埋下伏笔，

blocks.en_text: like depression and eventually Alzheimer's disease.
blocks.zh_text: 比如抑郁症，最终甚至可能导致阿尔茨海默病。

blocks.en_text: The effects of stress may filter right down to your brain's DNA.
blocks.zh_text: 压力的影响甚至可能一直深入到大脑的DNA。

blocks.en_text: An experiment showed
blocks.zh_text: 一项实验表明，

blocks.en_text: that the amount of nurturing a mother rat provides its newborn baby
blocks.zh_text: 母鼠对新生幼鼠的照料程度

blocks.en_text: plays a part in determining how that baby responds to stress later in life.
blocks.zh_text: 在一定程度上决定了这只幼鼠日后如何应对压力。

blocks.en_text: The pups of nurturing moms turned out less sensitive to stress
blocks.zh_text: 结果发现，被悉心照料的幼鼠对压力的敏感度更低

blocks.en_text: because their brains developed more cortisol receptors,
blocks.zh_text: 因为它们的大脑发育出了更多的皮质醇受体，

blocks.en_text: which stick to cortisol and dampen the stress response.
blocks.zh_text: 这些受体与皮质醇结合，从而抑制了压力反应。

blocks.en_text: The pups of negligent moms had the opposite outcome,
blocks.zh_text: 而被疏于照料的幼鼠则恰恰相反，

blocks.en_text: and so became more sensitive to stress throughout life.
blocks.zh_text: 因此它们一生中对压力都更加敏感。

blocks.en_text: These are considered epigenetic changes,
blocks.zh_text: 这些被认为是表观遗传变化，

blocks.en_text: meaning that they effect which genes are expressed
blocks.zh_text: 意思是它们会影响哪些基因被表达出来，

blocks.en_text: without directly changing the genetic code.
blocks.zh_text: 而不会直接改变遗传密码。

blocks.en_text: And these changes can be reversed if the moms are swapped.
blocks.zh_text: 而且如果把这些母鼠对调，这些变化是可以逆转的。

blocks.en_text: But there's a surprising result.
blocks.zh_text: 但还有一个令人惊讶的结果。

blocks.en_text: The epigenetic changes caused by one single mother rat
blocks.zh_text: 仅仅一只母鼠所造成的表观遗传变化，

blocks.en_text: were passed down to many generations of rats after her.
blocks.zh_text: 竟然遗传给了她之后的许多代老鼠。

blocks.en_text: In other words, the results of these actions were inheritable.
blocks.zh_text: 换句话说，这些行为的结果是可以遗传的。

blocks.en_text: It's not all bad news, though.
blocks.zh_text: 不过也不全是坏消息。

blocks.en_text: There are many ways to reverse what cortisol does to your stressed brain.
blocks.zh_text: 有很多方法可以逆转皮质醇对你受压大脑造成的影响。

blocks.en_text: The most powerful weapons are exercise and meditation,
blocks.zh_text: 最有力的武器是运动和冥想，

blocks.en_text: which involves breathing deeply
blocks.zh_text: 冥想包括深呼吸，

blocks.en_text: and being aware and focused on your surroundings.
blocks.zh_text: 以及觉察并专注于你周围的环境。

blocks.en_text: Both of these activities decrease your stress
blocks.zh_text: 这两种活动都能减轻你的压力，

blocks.en_text: and increase the size of the hippocampus,
blocks.zh_text: 并增大海马体的大小，

blocks.en_text: thereby improving your memory.
blocks.zh_text: 从而改善你的记忆力。

blocks.en_text: So don't feel defeated by the pressures of daily life.
blocks.zh_text: 所以，不要被日常生活的压力打败。

blocks.en_text: Get in control of your stress before it takes control of you.
blocks.zh_text: 在压力控制你之前，先掌控好你的压力。
